objective: Port netty-handler-proxy 4.2.19.Final (io.netty.handler.proxy: the HTTP CONNECT, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 proxy handlers) to Netty.NET.Handler.Proxy with the original names, structure, comments and tests, and an explicit evidence-backed record for each CLR adaptation and each unit that is not ported.

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

Owner decisions 2026-11-19 for the codec modules that only need codec-base: one project per Maven module; codec-socks is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Socks (its Maven and JPMS name) and holds the socks and socksx namespaces; haproxy is HAProxy (the casing of the Java types in that package); socksx, v4 and v5 are Socksx, V4 and V5.
2026-11-25: the project is Netty.NET.Handler.Proxy, the namespace root of io.netty.handler.proxy (the 2026-11-19 rule; no new name choice), and its tests are Netty.NET.Handler.Proxy.Tests.

statusMeaning.verified: Every declared original test is mapped to a C# test with the same name (case may differ) and passes.
statusMeaning.clr-adapted: Ported with the original names, structure and comments; every CLR difference is stated in a // CLR: comment and in this entry. For tests, some original methods are CLR-inapplicable with recorded evidence.
statusMeaning.deprecated-not-ported: @Deprecated Java unit (or a helper serving one) that is not ported; the deprecation facts, reason, replacement and every original comment/test are recorded.
statusMeaning.jvm-only-replaced: JVM-only metadata or documentation unit replaced by its recorded CLR counterpart.

review.scope: Sealed ProxyHandler subclass. The HTTP message interfaces take the I prefix (IFullHttpRequest, IHttpResponse, ILastHttpContent); CharSequence is ICharSequence; CharsetUtil.UTF_8/US_ASCII are Encoding.UTF8/ASCII and Unpooled.EMPTY_BUFFER is Unpooled.EmptyBuffer, as in codec-http. HttpProxyConnectException is the nested sealed class (serialVersionUID has no counterpart). HttpClientCodecWrapper implements IChannelInboundHandler and IChannelOutboundHandler and forwards every callback to the wrapped HttpClientCodec, whose ChannelPromise parameters are the Tasks the codec returns. The protected newInitialMessage, which HttpProxyHandlerTest calls through package access, has the internal forwarder InvokeNewInitialMessage (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Package access). HttpVersion is aliased to the codec-http type (System.Net.HttpVersion has the same name). SocketAddress is EndPoint, a resolved InetSocketAddress IPEndPoint and an unresolved one DnsEndPoint (docs/handler-porting.md, Addresses). "InetSocketAddress raddr = destinationAddress()" is ProxyHandler.CastToInetSocketAddress, which keeps an IPEndPoint, a DnsEndPoint or null and throws InvalidCastException (ClassCastException) for any other address; isUnresolved() is a DnsEndPoint, getHostString() its Host, getPort() the Port, and getAddress().getHostAddress() is ProxyHandler.GetHostAddress, the JDK text (uncompressed IPv6 groups) built as handler's IpSubnetFilterRule builds it.

java.net.ConnectException extends SocketException extends java.io.IOException (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/net/ConnectException.html). The CLR SocketException has no constructor that takes an inner exception (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.sockets.socketexception.-ctor?view=net-10.0), so a subclass could not keep the cause that the (Throwable) and (String, Throwable) constructors record with initCause; the class extends System.IO.IOException, which has IOException(String, Exception) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.ioexception?view=net-10.0), as the Transport's ClosedChannelException does. initCause(cause) is the base innerException; without a message Exception.Message is the system default where Java's getMessage() is null. serialVersionUID has no counterpart.

Sealed class; the generic <T extends SocketAddress> accessors are generic methods constrained to EndPoint (Java infers T from the assignment target, a C# caller names it; the cast is checked). checkNotNull is ObjectUtil.CheckNotNull and simpleClassName StringUtil.SimpleClassName; an address prints as EndPoint.ToString().

ChannelDuplexHandler subclass with the source state machine. The ChannelPromise of connect/write is the Task that ConnectAsync/WriteAsync return: a write before the handshake finishes returns the consumer Task of PendingWriteQueue.Add(msg, cancellationToken), removeAndWriteAll() is RemoveAndWriteAllAsync() with its Task ignored as in the source, removeAndFailAll keeps its role. Future<Channel> connectFuture() is Task<IChannel>; LazyChannelPromise (a DefaultPromise on ctx.executor()) is a TaskCompletionSource<IChannel> with RunContinuationsAsynchronously, as SslHandler maps its LazyChannelPromise. The write listener is a continuation on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (DefaultPromise.notifyListeners timing); the connect timeout is ctx.Executor.ScheduleAsync with TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds and a CancellationTokenSource for the Future (cancel(false) is Cancel()), as SslHandler/WriteTimeoutHandler do. promise.setFailure(new ConnectionPendingException()) is a Task faulted with SocketException(SocketError.AlreadyInProgress), the Transport's counterpart. C# has no volatile long, so connectTimeoutMillis uses Volatile.Read/Write (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.volatile?view=net-10.0). cause.toString() is ThrowableUtil.ThrowableToString (owner decision 2026-11-24); StringBuilder.append(null) writes "null" while the C# Append(object) writes nothing (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.stringbuilder.append?view=net-10.0), so an unset destination is written as "null" in exceptionMessage. catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception). The generic <T extends SocketAddress> accessors are generic methods constrained to EndPoint whose cast is checked. Final methods are sealed overrides or non-virtual; AUTH_NONE is internal const. SocketAddress is EndPoint, a resolved InetSocketAddress IPEndPoint and an unresolved one DnsEndPoint (docs/handler-porting.md, Addresses). "InetSocketAddress raddr = destinationAddress()" is ProxyHandler.CastToInetSocketAddress, which keeps an IPEndPoint, a DnsEndPoint or null and throws InvalidCastException (ClassCastException) for any other address; isUnresolved() is a DnsEndPoint, getHostString() its Host, getPort() the Port, and getAddress().getHostAddress() is ProxyHandler.GetHostAddress, the JDK text (uncompressed IPv6 groups) built as handler's IpSubnetFilterRule builds it.

Sealed ProxyHandler subclass on the codec-socks SOCKS5 types (the message interfaces take the I prefix). Java's byte is the C# byte of the codec-socks port (Socks5AuthMethod.ByteValue(), IsPrivateMethod(byte)), so privateAuthMethod & 0xFF keeps its value. Collections.singletonList and Arrays.asList are lists passed to the IEnumerable constructor of DefaultSocks5InitialRequest, the counterpart of its List constructor. The Socks5AuthMethod comparisons stay reference comparisons. java.lang.Error for the unreachable branch is InvalidOperationException, as codec-base's AsciiHeadersEncoder maps it; IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. The last res local sits in a block because C# rejects a local that a nested scope of the same method also declares (CS0136). caseMappings.adaptation: CLR-adapted expectation: new InetSocketAddress(InetAddress.getByName("localhost"), port) keeps the host name "localhost" for getHostString(), while IPEndPoint keeps only the IPAddress and HttpUtil.FormatHostnameForHttp returns its numeric text (codec-http HttpUtilTest.testFormatHostnameForHttpFromResolvedAddressWithHostname is CLR-inapplicable for the same reason). The test resolves localhost with DefaultNameResolver (InetAddress.getByName) and expects that numeric text (bracketed for IPv6) where the source expects "localhost", so the CONNECT URL and the Host header choice for the port are still checked.

Source scenarios, inputs and assertions in namespace Netty.NET.Handler.Proxy.Tests. InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved is DnsEndPoint and SocketUtils.socketAddress of a literal is new IPEndPoint(IPAddress.Parse(host), port) (docs/handler-porting.md, Addresses). InetAddress.getByName and new InetSocketAddress(host, port) resolve with Resolver's DefaultNameResolver, as Transport's AbstractBootstrap does. Mockito is Moq: the ChannelPromise of connect(ctx, remote, local, promise) is the CancellationToken the handler passes on, so same(promise) and verify(ctx).connect(proxyAddress, null, promise) match that token (Times.Once, the Mockito default); verifyNoMoreInteractions(promise) on the new mock checks no interaction and has no counterpart without a promise object. new DefaultHttpHeaders(false) is DefaultHttpHeadersFactory.HeadersFactory().WithValidation(false).NewHeaders() (codec-http HttpHeadersTest). The protected newInitialMessage is reached through the internal InvokeNewInitialMessage. @ValueSource(booleans) is [Theory] [InlineData]; sync() awaits the Tasks; the anonymous classes are nested classes and ActionChannelInitializer; AtomicBoolean/AtomicReference are Common's; IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. The EmbeddedChannel subclass that reads the captured AtomicBoolean is constructed before it stores the flag, so IsActive is false during the base constructor, as the new AtomicBoolean is.

Collections.shuffle(list, rnd) is the same swap walk over System.Random (a seed reproduces a C# order). b.connect(...).channel() is a channel factory that captures the new NioSocketChannel, because Bootstrap.ConnectAsync yields the channel only on success but calls the factory synchronously, as Transport's SocketCloseForciblySourceTest does; Future.await(timeout) is Task.WhenAny with Task.Delay (true when the Task completed in time); CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent with a guarded Signal (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.countdownevent.signal); java.lang.AssertionError is xUnit's FailException; isInstanceOf/assertInstanceOf are Assert.IsAssignableFrom; String.valueOf(e) is ThrowableUtil.ThrowableToString; java.net.ConnectException is the Transport's SocketException(SocketError.ConnectionRefused). The X509Bundle key pair is the certificate's AsymmetricAlgorithm and InsecureTrustManagerFactory.INSTANCE its validation callback, as in handler's CipherSuiteCanaryTest. The lifecycle methods are private (xUnit1013), assertEquals(1, size()) is Assert.Single (xUnit2013) and the channel operations receive TestContext.Current.CancellationToken (xUnit1051). The anonymous EmbeddedChannel subclass that reports an inactive channel is InactiveEmbeddedChannel; the Transport's lifecycle checks read the virtual IsActive as the source calls isActive() (docs/transport-porting.md), so its registration fires no channelActive, as in Java.
